title: Javascript Variables Exercise Start
summary: Introduces the next lesson's coding exercise: swap the values held by two variables under three constraints. The solution is explained in the following lecture.

concepts.heading: How the exercise is presented
points: The next lesson is an in-browser coding exercise with instructions on top and an editable code file below, plus a linked online sandbox (Repl.it) for experimenting. Check Solution validates the answer; Continue moves on to the walkthrough.
Starting code declares a as 3 and b as 8 and logs them. Running it unchanged prints a is 3 and b is 8.
A mental model: two buckets, one with sand and one with water; how do you exchange the contents?

code_examples.caption: (Extra) Starting situation, reconstructed

task.name: Swap two variables
task.starting_point: Two variables: a holds 3, b holds 8. Three blank lines (7 to 9) sit between the declarations and the logging.
task.goal: After your code, a must hold 8 and b must hold 3.
steps: Do not modify any existing line; add code only in the three free lines.
Do not type any numeric literals (so no a = 8 or b = 3).
Do not redeclare a or b with var/let/const.
Use the online sandbox to test, then enter the answer and press Check Solution.
task.expected_result: Console output reads a is 8 and b is 3.

pitfalls: Assigning a = b then b = a loses the original value of a, so both end up 8. A third holder is needed (see the solution lecture).

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet. Closest is s14-variables (14.3) which only covers declaring and reassigning.
gaps_and_ideas: Add a lesson 'Swap two variables' after Variables: blurb about reassigning without losing data.
Tasks: (1) make a=3,b=8 print swapped, (2) do it without typing numbers, (3) predict what a = b; b = a; produces, (4) optional: swap with destructuring [a, b] = [b, a].
Starter: let a = 3; let b = 8; with TODO lines and a check that asserts a === 8 and b === 3.
Interactive demo: two animated buckets showing each assignment step.
